drugs.name: Tirzepatide
drugs.mechanism: Dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and GLP-1 receptor agonist suppressing appetite and increasing energy expenditure
drugs.efficacy: Achieves >20% mean body weight reduction in chronic weight management
drugs.adverse_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, dyspepsia, decreased appetite

drugs.name: Semaglutide
drugs.mechanism: Selective GLP-1 receptor agonist acting centrally in hypothalamic arcuate nucleus to promote satiety
drugs.efficacy: Achieves ~15% mean body weight reduction and major cardiovascular risk reduction
drugs.adverse_effects: Nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation, abdominal pain, headache

drugs.name: Setmelanotide
drugs.mechanism: Melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) agonist restoring impaired satiety signaling in monogenic and syndromic obesity
drugs.efficacy: Substantial weight loss and hyperphagia reduction in POMC, PCSK1, LEPR, and Bardet-Biedl syndrome obesity
drugs.adverse_effects: Skin hyperpigmentation, injection site reactions, nausea, headache

drugs.name: Phentermine / Topiramate
drugs.mechanism: Sympathomimetic amine appetite suppressant combined with GABAergic/AMPA neuroactive agent
drugs.efficacy: Effective chronic weight reduction (~8-10% at one year)
drugs.adverse_effects: Paresthesias, dry mouth, insomnia, constipation, tachycardia, teratogenic risk
